# My Plan for This Season

Alright, let me think through this properly. I've got 15 mu total. My wife and I are the only labor we've got, and at 60 neither of us moves as fast as we used to, so I have to be honest with myself about what we can handle. Over the years I've settled on splitting the land: about **10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation** and **5 mu in cotton**. The wheat-maize is the backbone — it feeds us and gives steady cash. The cotton is for cash, but it's the crop that demands the most from my back, especially at picking time, so I keep it limited.

## Wheat (10 mu, the autumn crop I'm planning for this October)

Based on my soil — it's the typical fluvo-aquic ground around here, and I've been building it up with straw return for years — I'm targeting about **480 kg/mu**. That's realistic for my fields; I hit 500 two years ago but last year the spring wind knocked some down. I'll plant **Jimai 22** around **October 10-15**, right when the topsoil temperature settles. I've saved some of my own seed but for wheat I buy certified every two or three years to keep quality up.

For N, I work it out from the yield target: 18 kg N/mu total, split about **60% as base compound fertilizer and 40% as urea topdress at jointing**. Base goes in with the seed — a 15-15-15 compound at around 40 kg/mu gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K, then I'll top that with urea at green-up/jointing in early March. If the wheat looks dark and thick I'll hold back; if it looks pale and thin I'll push the topdress to 12 kg. That's how I read the crop — the color tells me more than any book.

Irrigation: **3 times** is my plan — once before winter to seal it in (early December), green-up (March), and grain-filling (early May). If the spring is wet I'll skip one. Pumping isn't cheap, and the water table keeps dropping, so I don't waste water.

Weeds I spray once in early spring with a broadleaf herbicide. Aphids I watch for in April — only spray if I see them on the flag leaves.

## Maize (10 mu, same ground, summer crop after wheat)

Wheat harvest is around **June 10-12**. The combine comes and within three days I'm planting maize directly into the stubble — no time for tillage, it's straw return and direct-drill. I use **Zhengdan 958** or whatever hybrid the neighbors got good results with last year. The turnaround is so tight there's no room for trying anything clever.

N rate for maize: **16 kg N/mu**, mostly as a **one-shot side-dress at the big trumpet stage** (V10-V12, around late July). I used to split it but honestly the one-shot works nearly as well and saves me a pass through the field. Compound fertilizer at planting for starter P and K.

Irrigation for maize: usually **1 time around silking** if July-August is dry. If we get good summer rain I skip it entirely. Last year I didn't irrigate maize at all and still got 510 kg/mu.

Pesticide: pre-emergence herbicide for sure (atrazine mix), and I scout for corn borer — one spray if needed.

Expected yield: **500 kg/mu**.

## Cotton (5 mu)

Cotton is where my experience really pays off, and where I earn most of my cash. Plant **around April 20-25** on raised beds I prepared after winter plowing. I use a **Bt hybrid** — bollworm used to ruin us before Bt cotton came in, now it's manageable.

Fertilizer for cotton: **15 kg N, 6 kg P, 8 kg K per mu**. Cotton wants its potassium or the bolls don't fill. I split N in three — base, first flower, peak flowering. Topping the plants by hand at the right time matters more than people think; I still do that myself.

Irrigate **twice**: once at first flower, once at peak bloom. Pesticide is the real expense — **herbicide, aphid/mite sprays, and a defoliant** before picking. Cotton gets maybe 4-5 spray passes over the season.

Picking is the hard part. My wife and I can't pick 5 mu alone anymore, so I'll **hire 2-3 people for about a week** in September-October. That's 2000 yuan right there, but there's no way around it.

Expected lint yield: **280 kg/mu**.

## What I'm worried about this year

Two things. First, **urea prices** have been creeping up — if they jump again I'll trim the maize topdress by 2 kg/mu and accept slightly less yield. Second, my **well is 80 meters deep now** — it was 40 when I started farming. Every year pumping costs more. This is why I'm careful about irrigation timing, not generous.
